subject: append to list by factor / fast aggregation

messages.author: e135b7b3e4ed39d1
messages.subject: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have a long vector of numbers x and a vector Cats denoting which category each number belongs to. I'd like to aggregate x by Cats in base R, and was thinking of using lapply. Is there a fast way to create a list where elements of x belonging to different Cats would be in different list entries?

Example: x=1:10, Cats=rep(1:3,c(3,3,4)), and the resulting list looks like x.list=list(rep(1,3),rep(2,3),rep(3,4)). Then I could do lapply(x.list,sum).

Would love to hear alternative suggestions; my only preference is for base R and speed (I'll need to aggregate 10,000-long vectors billions of times).

Many thanks and happy new year!

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
parts:
Don't know about the speed, but here's a base-R solution, using the
"by" function (which is a wrapper for the "tapply" function).
Bottom line:

> lapply(x.list,sum) ## from the statement of the problem

[[1]]
[1] 3

[[2]]
[1] 6

[[3]]
[1] 12

> sums_list ## from the proposed solution
$`1`
[1] 3

$`2`
[1] 6

$`3`
[1] 12

## Original example

x <- 1:10
x

Cats <- rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))
Cats

x.list <- list(rep(1,3),rep(2,3),rep(3,4))
x.list

lapply(x.list,sum)

## Possible solution

df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
df

sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
sum(grp["Cats"])
})
sums_by ## object of class "by"

sums_list <- as.list(sums_by)
sums_list ## object of class "list"

messages.author: 47ca46208a81ec5e
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
parts:
If I’m understanding you right, you can use split() to do this:

x.list = split(x, Cats)
lapply(x.list,sum)

I guessed that using tapply() directly would be fastest, but it appears the split() then lapply() is faster!

Did you mean for your sum() operation to not involve the x vector at all? Right now, your result suggests that you want to sum the numbers corresponding to the category labels. That is, x.list is the same as Cats but just diced up a little differently. If this is what you want, then use the split() function with Cats as both arguments (split(Cats, Cats))

library(microbenchmark)

x=1:10
Cats = rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))

microbenchmark(aggregate = aggregate(x, list(Cats), FUN = sum), 
               tapply = tapply(X = x, INDEX = Cats, FUN = sum),
               hannon = { df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
                          sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
                            sum(grp["Cats"])
                          })
                          sums_list <- as.list(sums_by)
                        },
               hannon_stay_as_by = { df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
               sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
                 sum(grp["Cats"])
               })
               },
               split = {  x.list = split(x, Cats)
                          lapply(x.list,sum)}
               )
## Unit: microseconds
##               expr     min       lq       mean    median        uq
##          aggregate 576.872 603.2775  710.40752  624.3805  689.9060
##             tapply  79.339  93.8830  112.41990  104.1095  115.8365
##             hannon 571.793 597.6665 1513.54809  870.8985 1777.5830
##  hannon_stay_as_by 569.428 585.4495 1303.66409 1263.2130 1757.3600
##              split  52.606  64.0900   72.45376   71.8240   76.9565
##        max neval cld
##   2833.339   100  b 
##    365.627   100 a  
##  17538.522   100   c
##   4344.227   100   c
##    117.059   100 a

Maybe there’s an even faster way though?

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
parts:
I hope it works out as much as I understand your query...
best of luck..

x=1:10
Cats=rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))
df.cats = data.frame(X= x,  Cats=Cats) # create data frame
df.cats$Cats = as.factor(df.cats$Cats) # turn Cats  into a factor
nlevel = length(levels(df.cats$Cats)) # count how many levels you have
vecAggregate = vector(length = nlevel) # declare aggregate  vector of nlevel
for (i in 1:nlevel){
  df1 = subset(df.cats, Cats==i) # use subset function to extract information at each level
  vecAggregate[i] = sum(df1[,1]) # aggregate at each level
}
